title: Recovering Strongly Connected Components in Equal-Variance Gaussian Feedback Models
banked_reason: The explicit seven-vertex pair has equal labeled outdegrees and perfect matchings in all fourteen local Hall graphs but different SCC partitions, so the universal positive implication is false.
gap_reasons: The explicit seven-vertex pair has equal labeled outdegrees and perfect matchings in all fourteen local Hall graphs but different SCC partitions, so the universal positive implication is false.
REVIEW: assume-the-crux narrowing — a new assume/suppose premise may promote the open obligation into a hypothesis (state the result and leave the construction an open obligation instead).
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted to prove the all-size two-sided Hall-compatibility theorem H★ and use it as the universal separator supporting generic SCC recovery. The solver instead produced a verified seven-vertex oriented-simple counterexample with equal labeled outdegrees, zero Hall deficiency in both orders, and different SCC partitions; the independent validity gate confirmed that replacing H★ by a familywise separation assumption would only assume the missing conclusion. Unequal-outdegree and positive-deficiency cases remain valid sufficient cases, while a genuinely different universal precision/Jacobian separator is open.
tldr: For labeled noncomplete simple orientations with a common Gaussian structural error variance, the proposal reduces every comparator-parent closed child-count certificate to a Hall deficiency, proves that the certificate creates an explicit precision-Jacobian rank gap, and targets the universal H-star theorem that two-sided local perfect matchings force equal SCC partitions. Conditional on H-star, the published unequal-outdegree separator yields a generic minimum-dimension covariance-model functional for feedback modules. On fixed finite compact families, cross-SCC covariance-image separation and an upper covariance-eigenvalue bound yield uniform covariance minimum-distance recovery; separate stability, edge, and scale restrictions describe the prospective SEM family but do not enter the displayed recovery bound. Split-sample procedures give honest sets of SCC partitions and union sets for equilibrium perfect-intervention effects between distinct vertices.
gap: Static Gaussian feedback models lack a complete, polynomially certified separator for the SCC partition when two orientations have equal labeled outdegrees. The closest paper isolates this boundary as Conjecture 5.1 and proves only an acyclic-side special case.
fill: The focal theorem is H-star, supported by the closure-to-Hall equality and the incoming-star rank minor. Conditional on proving H-star, it turns algebraic separation into a generic SCC recovery map. On fixed finite compact covariance families, the statistical bound depends on cross-SCC separation and the upper covariance-eigenvalue bound, while split-sample inversion propagates uncertainty to SCC partitions and distinct-vertex equilibrium effects.
